# Results — Study 668 (Williams VIX Fix)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Larry
Williams' **VIX Fix**, `WVF = (highest_close(22) - low) / highest_close(22) * 100`, a
synthetic fear gauge built from price alone — **spikes at capitulation bottoms; buy the
spike.** Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current
month is dropped). Basket fingerprints: `ff6a728ebf89` (SPY) / `dc33a4d14e22` (QQQ) /
`1dd0a989ecb9` (IWM) / `a1278fc100bc` (AAPL) / `0dcc0426245d` (MSFT) / `ccf94046c951` (JPM)
/ `9907d9f69d09` (XOM) / `62ea82f560f2` (JNJ).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily split+dividend-adjusted OHLC, 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30 (IWM from 2000-05-26 inception), 8 tickers, ~6,600 rows each |
| Basket | **SPY, QQQ, IWM** (broad index ETFs — no survivorship) + **AAPL, MSFT, JPM, XOM, JNJ** (five large, currently-listed single names — **survivorship named**: picked for a long clean tape, so any bounce this basket shows can only be a bounce in names that lived to tell about it) |
| Indicator | WVF(22) = (highest close over 22 sessions − low) / highest close × 100; spike = onset of WVF ≥ 20-session mean + 2×std of itself (the canonical Bollinger trigger) — one entry per capitulation episode |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal known at close *t*; enter at *t+1*'s **open**; exit at the close *h* sessions after entry. Round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV (5 / 10 bps) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* (pooled basket, primary); per-ticker Newey-West (HAC, lags = horizon) dummy regression as the overlap-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 500-draw random-calendar placebo; a two-dummy HAC regression against a plain close-only drawdown-proxy sibling for the third axis |
| Data quirks (named) | IWM's tape starts 2000-05-26 (its actual inception), 101 sessions shorter than the rest of the basket; all bars are yfinance `auto_adjust=True` (splits + dividends folded into price) |

## The headline — WVF-spike forward return vs unconditional, by horizon

| horizon | *n* spike episodes | spike mean | rest mean | gap | Welch *t* | hit rate | per-ticker NW *t* (mean, range) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d | 3,783 | +26.3 bps | +16.7 bps | +9.6 bps | **+1.33** | 56.3% (Wilson [54.7%, 57.9%]) | +0.59, [−0.73, **+2.38**] |
| 10d | 3,782 | +29.9 bps | +38.7 bps | **−8.8 bps** | **−0.88** | 55.3% (Wilson [53.7%, 56.9%]) | −0.11, [−1.57, +0.95] |
| 20d | 3,765 | +57.8 bps | +81.6 bps | **−23.9 bps** | **−1.74** | 58.6% (Wilson [57.0%, 60.2%]) | −0.33, [−1.48, +0.32] |

No horizon clears the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar in the claimed direction. At 5 days the pooled
gap is faintly positive but far short of significant (*t* = +1.33); by 10 and 20 days the
*sign flips* — WVF-spike days go on to underperform an unconditional day, and 20-day comes
closest to significant of the three, in the **wrong direction** (*t* = −1.74). Two names
(SPY *t* = +2.44, QQQ *t* = +3.08 — not shown in the pooled row above, see per-ticker table)
individually clear the bar **at 5 days only** — with 8 tickers × 3 horizons = 24 tests run,
seeing 2 cross ±2 by chance is unremarkable (≈1.2 expected at a nominal 5% two-sided rate),
and neither survives to 10 or 20 days. This is the signature of noise, not signal.

| MSFT | 435 | **−20.1 bps** | +38.5 bps | **−2.24** | −1.57 | 49.4% |
| JPM | 449 | +53.1 bps | +33.9 bps | +0.56 | +0.37 | 54.3% |

MSFT is the one name whose Welch *t* clears ±2 at 10 days — and it is **negative**: buying
its WVF spikes *underperforms* an unconditional MSFT day. No ticker shows a significant
*positive* 10-day edge.

## Random-calendar placebo (h = 10, pooled)

20 seeds × 500 draws (10,000 total) of 3,782 random non-spike days from the pooled basket:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spike-day mean | +29.9 bps |
| placebo mean (sd) | +38.8 bps (7.8 bps) |
| *p*-value (right-tail: share of random calendars ≥ observed) | **0.874** |

The observed WVF-spike mean is **beaten by 87.4% of purely random 3,782-day calendars** —
the opposite of what a real edge would show. This is not a rounding-error near-miss; the
spike days are unremarkable at best.

## Third axis — is WVF more than a plain close-only drawdown proxy? (h = 10)

A sibling indicator built the same way but from the **close alone** — no intrabar low —
`drawdown(22) = (highest_close(22) − close) / highest_close(22) × 100`, same 20/2σ
Bollinger trigger. A two-dummy HAC regression `fwd_10 ~ a + b·onset(WVF) + c·onset(drawdown)`
isolates the marginal value of the wick, controlling for the plain drawdown signal fired on
the same day.

| ticker | overlap (WVF ⊂ drawdown) | marginal WVF *t* | marginal drawdown *t* | WVF-only mean | drawdown-only mean | Welch *t* (diff) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 74.1% | −0.04 | +0.88 | +10.8 bps | +35.1 bps | −0.58 |
| QQQ | 75.9% | −0.41 | +2.02 | +34.3 bps | +98.2 bps | −1.29 |
| IWM | 76.1% | −0.86 | +1.12 | −50.5 bps | +24.6 bps | −1.13 |
| AAPL | 72.2% | −0.91 | +0.23 | +10.5 bps | +88.2 bps | −0.75 |
| MSFT | 74.9% | −1.66 | −0.06 | −23.7 bps | +33.3 bps | −1.02 |
| JPM | 76.8% | +0.68 | −0.52 | +70.6 bps | +12.8 bps | +0.65 |
| XOM | 75.2% | −0.07 | −0.37 | +26.9 bps | +15.1 bps | +0.17 |
| JNJ | 78.3% | +0.89 | −0.82 | +37.9 bps | +0.1 bps | +0.83 |
| **basket avg** | **75.5%** | **−0.30** | **+0.31** | | | |

Three quarters of every WVF spike is a day the plain close-only drawdown proxy would have
flagged anyway. The marginal WVF contribution — the intrabar wick's own information, over
and above "price is far below its 22-day high" — averages *t* = **−0.30** across the
basket: not one name shows a significant *positive* marginal WVF effect, and in 5 of 8 names
the WVF-only subset actually underperforms the drawdown-only subset (though none of those
differences clear ±2 either). The wick the VIX Fix is built to capture adds nothing this
basket can detect.

## The timer — buy every WVF-spike onset, hold 10 sessions, costs charged

| cost | *n* trades | net mean | win rate | Sharpe/trade | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | 3,782 | +29.9 bps | 55.3% | 0.050 | +1.76 |
| 5 bps one-way | 3,782 | +19.9 bps | 54.4% | 0.033 | +1.17 |
| 10 bps one-way | 3,782 | +9.9 bps | 53.1% | 0.016 | +0.58 |

Even **before** costs the pooled ledger doesn't clear *t* ≥ 2 (+1.76); one round trip at 5
bps one-way nearly halves the point estimate and drops the HAC *t* to +1.17; at 10 bps it's
statistically indistinguishable from zero. Per-ticker (net, 5 bps): SPY *t* = +1.32, QQQ
*t* = +1.52, IWM *t* = +0.06, AAPL *t* = +0.25, MSFT *t* = −0.76, JPM *t* = +0.77, XOM
*t* = +0.22, JNJ *t* = +1.28 — no name reaches the bar.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic OHLC generator with occasional violent one-day crashes (a wide low-wick — the
exact geometry WVF hunts for) and a TUNABLE planted post-crash bounce; no network. Primary
detector: the Newey-West *t* (lags = 10, matching the forward-return overlap).

| world | Welch *t* | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (bounce = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.29** (sd 1.22), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 | mean **−0.18** (sd 0.82), **\|*t*\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** |
| planted bounce = +0.002/day × 10 sessions (seed 668) | **+3.54** | **+2.47** |

The Newey-West detector never fires on the null across 20 independent seeds and lights up
cleanly on a planted bounce; the raw Welch statistic fires once in 20 (consistent with its
nominal ~5% two-sided false-positive rate on a single-draw test, not miscalibration). The
harness can find a real capitulation-bounce effect when one is planted — it does not find
one on the real tape. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of
the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No horizon (5/10/20d) clears **t ≥ 2** in the claimed direction on the
  pooled basket (+1.33 / −0.88 / −1.74); the sign flips negative by 10 days and the
  20-day gap is the closest to significant of the three — in the wrong direction. The
  10-day placebo shows the observed spike-day mean losing to 87.4% of random calendars.
  Two names look real at 5 days alone (SPY *t* = +2.44, QQQ *t* = +3.08) but that's ≈1.2
  false positives expected from 24 raw tests, and neither survives to 10 or 20 days —
  the one ticker that *does* clear ±2 at 10 days (MSFT) does so with the **wrong sign**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even gross of any cost the pooled 10-day timer doesn't clear
  *t* ≥ 2 (+1.76); 5 bps one-way costs drop it to +1.17, 10 bps to +0.58. There is no
  residual edge for costs to eat — the mirage is visible before you even model the spread.
- **"More than a drawdown proxy?" — BUSTED.** 75.5% of every WVF spike is a day a plain
  close-only "how far below the 22-day high" flag would have caught anyway, and the
  intrabar wick's marginal contribution (controlling for that plain proxy) averages
  *t* = −0.30 across the basket — indistinguishable from zero, occasionally negative. The
  VIX-Fix formula's extra ingredient — the low, not just the close — buys nothing a
  simpler drawdown filter didn't already have.
